top.title: UK privacy watchdog faces probe into its workplace culture
top.description: Britain's privacy watchdog is getting a taste of its own medicine, with an independent review set to examine the culture, governance, and accountability surrounding the events that led to former Information Commissioner John Edwards' resignation. Karon Monaghan KC will examine whether the regulator's culture and governance allowed problems to develop or made concerns harder to raise. Edwards quit in June after an independent workplace investigation found there was a "case to answer" over his behavior and that his conduct fell short of what was expected of a public official. He disagreed with some of its findings, but ultimately conceded that he had shown "poor judgment." That investigation, however, focused on Edwards alone. According to the terms of reference published on Thursday, it "did not consider the wider conditions in which that conduct occurred, and it was not designed to." The new review will cast a wider net. Monaghan wants to know whether staff could call out bad behavior further up the food chain, and what awaited those who tried. It will also poke around the regulator's leadership and governance arrangements and its relationship with its sponsoring government department, including whether there were adequate ways for concerns to be escalated and those at the top to be challenged. Current and former staff can give evidence confidentially and voluntarily, while Monaghan will be given access to relevant documents and existing material, including staff surveys and data on bullying, harassment and discrimination. The ICO has confirmed it won't use confidentiality clauses in settlement agreements to prevent people from contributing to the review. Monaghan decides which witnesses and documents are relevant, rather than the ICO or DCMS. Access remains subject to legal restrictions, and she must be told when material is withheld and why. She can speak to whoever she thinks is relevant and ask for the complaints, correspondence, and other paperwork she needs. And if that leads her somewhere unexpected, she can ask to widen the investigation. DCMS can refuse, but it won't be able to quietly brush the request aside, and any decision not to expand the scope has to make it into the final report. The review won't reopen the investigation into Edwards, make findings about the conduct of named individuals, or delve into the merits of the regulator's enforcement decisions. Its arrival comes amid a broader shake-up at Britain's data watchdog. The old Information Commissioner's Office was formally replaced by the Information Commission on September 30, bringing with it a new board-led governance model. The government first promised the wider review in July, shortly after Edwards' departure, but it didn't appoint its reviewer or nail down the terms until late November. top.title: Delta attack: PANDEF writes IGP, DSS DG, demands probe
top.description: By Henry Umoru ABUJA — The Pan Niger Delta Forum (PANDEF) has written to the Inspector-General of Police, Olatunji Disu, and the Director-General of the Department of State Services (DSS), Oluwatosin Ajayi, demanding an urgent investigation into the reported violence at a political rally in Ughelli, Delta State. The socio-political organisation called on both security chiefs to work with other relevant agencies to identify and prosecute those who allegedly planned, sponsored, instigated or participated in the attack on the campaign train of former Deputy President of the Senate, Senator Ovie Omo-Agege. Omo-Agege, who is the All Progressives Congress (APC) senatorial candidate for Delta Central, was reportedly attacked during a campaign rally on Monday, November 23, 2026, with some persons said to have been killed and several others injured. In a letter signed by its National Chairman, Ambassador Godknows Igali, PANDEF strongly condemned the incident and described the reported loss of lives and injuries as disturbing and unacceptable. The organisation also urged the Federal Government, relevant federal agencies and the Delta State Government to provide financial and other forms of assistance to families of those reportedly killed, as well as adequate medical care for the injured. In the letter, PANDEF said it was shocked by reports of violence at a political rally organised by the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) in parts of Uduere, Delta State, on Monday. It, however, noted that the reports of deaths and injuries had yet to be officially corroborated. “According to media reports, which are yet to be officially corroborated, some persons reportedly lost their lives, while several others sustained varying degrees of injuries. We consider these reported incidents extremely disturbing and totally unacceptable,” the letter stated. PANDEF recalled that it had issued a statement the previous week warning against political violence, intimidation and intolerance of opposition parties in the South-South. It said the latest incident, coming days after its appeal, was a source of grave concern, adding that the region had traditionally upheld political tolerance, sportsmanship and civility. The organisation further warned that insecurity in the South-South could have implications beyond the region, given its strategic importance to Nigeria’s oil and gas industry and national economy. “Any disruption of peace and security in the region, particularly violence associated with political and electoral activities, could have far-reaching implications, not only for the safety and wellbeing of our people but also for the stability and economic survival of the country,” it said. top.title: Jude Bellingham stands up for female reporter after male colleague interrupts her in post-match interview
top.description: A clip of Jude Bellingham standing up for a female reporter who was interrupted during a post-match interview has gone viral. BBC Sport ’s Spanish football reporter Elizabeth Conway attempted to ask Bellingham a follow-up question in the mixed zone - where media gather to interview players - after asking him about his second-half goal in Real Madrid ’s 5-1 win over PSV Eindhoven on Tuesday. Her second question was interrupted by a male reporter, leading Bellingham to say, “Sorry, she's got one more”, before answering Conway’s follow-up. The clip of the interview spread widely on social media after the Champions League game, which meant Real Madrid - who had gone 1-0 down in the first half before storming back - extended their 100% winning record in this season’s league phase. Jude Bellingham with his second assist of the night 🤝 pic.twitter.com/IIkEKC6SNs — Match of the Day (@BBCMOTD) November 25, 2026 Conway told BBC Radio WM the mixed zone is “utter carnage” and can be “intimidating” as one of few women working in sports media, saying: “You've got elbows you've got microphones, you've got cameras, you've got massive tall men reaching over you. “I'm one of very, very, few female reporters and one of very, very, few English reporters there, so trying to make a stand for yourself and get in a good position is so important.” Of Bellingham’s interjection, she said: “It's shown him yet again being respectful, polite, and really respecting me as a journalist.” The 23-year-old was widely praised on social media for how he handled the situation, with comments reading “A whole lot of class” and “a role model for young men”. Bellingham scored in the 60th minute and provided the assist for Vinicius Junior ’s late goal, with Federico Valverde and Kylian Mbappe , who scored a brace, also on the scoresheet. The England star was part of a triple change at half-time and made an immediate impact, with his inventive goal coming from a touch with his left foot before he chipped it up with his right and volleyed home from 25 yards. Real Madrid top the group stage standings after five games played.

top.title: Ireland to make historic first-ever tour of Pakistan, six-match series confirmed
top.description: Ireland are set to make history in January 2027 when their men's side tours Pakistan for the first time, with a six-match 50-over series scheduled in Lahore as part of their preparations for the ICC World Cup Qualifier. Cricket Ireland on Thursday confirmed that the team will arrive in Pakistan on January 9 for a series running from January 13 to 24, with all six matches to be played at the Gaddafi Stadium in Lahore. The tour will comprise three 50-over matches against Pakistan A, known as the Shaheens, followed by a three-match ODI series against the senior Pakistan side. The matches will be played on January 13, 15 and 17 against the Shaheens, before the two teams meet in the ODIs on January 20, 22 and 24. Match timings are yet to be confirmed. While this will be the first visit to Pakistan by the Ireland men's side, it will not be the first tour by an Irish cricket team. The Ireland women's side visited the country in 2022 and famously won the T20I series. World Cup Qualifier preparations behind Ireland's tour The six-match assignment assumes particular significance for Ireland as they prepare for the ICC World Cup Qualifier in February 2027, which will be held in South Africa and Namibia. Graeme West, Cricket Ireland's Director of High Performance, underlined the importance of the tour in providing the one-day squad with valuable match practice ahead of the qualification campaign. “This is an extremely important tour for our One-Day squad as they prepare for the ICC World Cup Qualifiers in February. Following the nine games played in the second half of 2026, a further six 50-over matches against quality opponents will support the players readiness for the qualifier taking place in South Africa and Namibia. “While we originally planned a multi-format series, both Boards have agreed that their respective squads would benefit most from playing 50-over cricket given our upcoming participation in the World Cup Qualifier and Pakistan preparing for the World Cup itself later in 2027. “Over the years we have enjoyed a close relationship with the Pakistan Cricket Board and their players, and we look forward to this historic first tour – the first of many in the coming years, we hope.” The Pakistan Cricket Board had initially planned a triangular series involving Ireland, Pakistan and Zimbabwe. However, Zimbabwe subsequently withdrew, citing its inability to travel to Pakistan. The revised arrangement will see Ireland play two separate three-match assignments instead. Ireland-Pakistan ODI rivalry Ireland and Pakistan have faced each other seven times in men's ODIs, with Pakistan winning five matches, Ireland claiming one victory and one encounter ending in a tie. Ireland's only win remains one of the most memorable results in its cricketing history. It came during the 2007 World Cup in the Caribbean, when Ireland stunned Pakistan to knock the former champions out of the tournament. top.title: Tinubu willing to grant more interviews to Nigerian journalists — Bwala
top.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Special Adviser to the President on Media and Policy Communication, Daniel Bwala, has said President Bola Tinubu is willing to grant more interviews to Nigerian journalists, while maintaining that the Presidency will decide which media organisations interview him. Bwala said this during an interview on the Niger Unfiltered podcast, published on Thursday, following questions about why Tinubu had granted only one official interview to Nigerian media organisations in about three years and seven months in office. “I expect us to do more. And the second time, you’ll see more of that,” Bwala said. He acknowledged that some interviews had been postponed at short notice, saying the President had sometimes agreed to meet journalists before later rescheduling. “There are a number of times in which the President called for media. At the 11th hour, he may have been advised, and then he would apologise and say some other time,” Bwala said. The presidential aide said Tinubu was willing to speak with journalists and did not need prepared answers or prior briefings before interviews. “There is a willingness to grant interviews on the part of the President. And the President, when granting interviews, didn’t need to read anything, didn’t need to be briefed,” he said. Bwala defended the Presidency’s right to choose the journalists and platforms it engages, saying it should not be pressured to grant interviews to specific media organisations. “We control our narrative. We decide who we grant interviews to. Nobody can come and tell us, grant to this one and not the other one,” he said. He said State House press corps members representing mainstream, new, social and print media covered the President’s daily activities. “In the State House press corps, we have representatives of the mainstream, the new media, the social media, and the print media. So every day, the activity of the President is covered by them,” Bwala said. He also criticised some media practitioners over what he described as political bias and a lack of professionalism, arguing that Tinubu should engage journalists capable of conducting balanced interviews. Bwala’s remarks followed criticism of Tinubu’s recent interview with American political strategist and media personality Diana London. Some Nigerians questioned why the President had granted an interview to a foreign media personality while rarely speaking with Nigerian journalists. The controversy grew after reports linked London to a $4.5 million lobbying arrangement involving a United States-based firm engaged by the Nigerian government. London denied receiving the money from the Federal Government or anyone in Nigeria, saying she travelled to Nigeria to interview Tinubu for a documentary. top.title: How a baseball coach helped build a national esports contender at Choctaw
top.description: For Oklahoma’s Choctaw High School esports team, everything has happened pretty quickly. At the beginning of last school year, the newly minted program had a few students trickling in, some interest here and there. Just one season later, the Yellowjackets are ranked No. 25 in the nation and sitting at fourth in the USA TODAY Sports esports national title race. Talk about a bit of a jump. “It’s just kind of finding the right pieces to put the puzzle together,” said head coach Tim Ackerman, who has built the team up over the past year. “Everyone here has been super, super helpful every step of the way.” Ackerman spent years as a high school baseball coach, a role he still reprises each spring, before taking up the mantle as Choctaw’s inaugural esports leader. He’s infused some of that more traditional coaching experience, namely his emphasis on competitive practice, into his new role. “I’ve got really good gamers here who know a lot about their games, play their games well. But when it comes down to it, I think competing is a very important gap that a lot of schools miss on,” Ackerman said. “Understanding how to control momentum, how to control your emotions as you go…a professional approach when you’re going into a match, rather than just you’re at home with a controller.” View this post on Instagram It took a minute for the program to find its footing, but over time, students who might not have been attracted to it at first glance started to trickle in. They’d pop their heads into Ackerman’s room, telling him about their favorite games and scoring invites to “show me what you got” as he collected the right players for the team. Senior Blake Wallace, the team’s "Marvel Rivals" captain, was convinced to give it a shot though it did take second. “When I saw it my sophomore year in the classes you could take, I was like, ‘Only nerds are going to take that. I’m not going to do that,” Wallace said. But he came around. Now as a captain, he’s helped chart the course for the ever-growing squad. “My favorite part is that we’re always improving,” he said. “We do things where we go through games we lost and just break down everything we did wrong, and what we could do better next game.” The success and popularity of Choctaw’s esports squad has already extended to the middle school level, where Ackerman said nearly 70 students tried out for the small number of spots available on the Choctaw teams there. “I think the future is pretty bright over here,” he said. “There’s a lot of really excited, good players coming in, showing interest and wanting to be a part of it.” Meet the Choctaw team "Rocket League" Talan Wilkins Marco Torres Matthew Hernandez "Marvel Rivals" Grayson Cornelius Jaxon Buckingham Nik Hofmaier Daryl Knauer Sean Grizzle Blake Wallace "Madden NFL 27" Dashaun Taylor This article originally appeared on USA TODAY: How a baseball coach helped build a national esports contender at Choctaw

top.title: Arsenal send scouts to watch Champions League winger
top.description: Arsenal send scouts to watch Champions League winger Arsenal sent scouts to watch Antonio Nusa again in midweek, as the RB Leizpig winger scored a Champions League brace against RC Lens. Photo by Maja Hitij/Getty Images Graeme Bailey reports for TEAMtalk that Arsenal had representatives in attendance to watch RB Leipzig’s match against RC Lens on Tuesday evening, with Antonio Nusa proving the star of the show. Nusa scored Leipzig’s second and third goals in a 3-1 win, keeping his team’s hopes of progression to the knockout stages alive. Arsenal weren’t the only ones with scouts at the game, with Tottenham Hotspur , Chelsea , and Manchester City also sending representatives, as well as other top clubs from the continent. Bailey adds that Leipzig also have no intention of selling mid-season, believing they’re still in the Bundesliga title race, and attempting to convince the player to extend his existing 2029 contract. Photo by Maja Hitij/Getty Images Fabrizio Romano previously reported that Leipzig will be asking for around €70-75m (£58.5-62.7m) for Nusa, but that would be in the summer transfer window. It would need to be a ‘completely crazy’ bid to let him go in January. Romano has also confirmed that Arsenal are one of the clubs monitoring Nusa, with their scouts regularly watching the player’s development. Simon Collings had written in early November that Arsenal were tracking Nusa, though he was similarly clear that a deal in the winter window will be hard to pull off. Leipzig are under no financial pressure to sell mid-season, following Yan Diomande’s big-money move to Real Madrid . Photo by Boris Streubel/Getty Images 21-year-old winger Nusa is having an excellent season so far, with 17 direct goal contributions in his 17 appearances. Three of his goals have come in his five Champions League games, including one against Arsenal’s title rivals Manchester City . Arsenal have been keeping an eye on Nusa for quite a while now, with reports initially emerging in 2023 , when the player was still with Club Brugge. It looks like a move might now be possible in 2027, but it may have to wait for the summer. Photo by Alexander Hassenstein/Getty Images

top.description: Credit: Ashley Tumlin-Imagn Images The No. 7 Miami Hurricanes stand on the brink of history this Saturday. A win against Boston College would mark the program’s first-ever sweep of the Atlantic Coast Conference regular season. The Hurricanes hold a perfect 8-0 record inside the league, while their 10-1 overall record keeps them firmly in the hunt for the College Football Playoff. They face a Boston College team that sits at 5-6 and desperately needs a victory to reach bowl eligibility. The matchup against Boston College does not carry the heavy weight on Miami, already securing a spot in the ACC championship game in Charlotte on Dec. 5. Miami has been nearly flawless all season, but one loss to Notre Dame on Nov. 7 still stings. The offense has found ways to score without its star receiver, Malachi Toney, who has missed the last three games with an ankle injury. Quarterback Darian Mensah has stepped up with 3,317 passing yards and 29 touchdowns this year. His performance has earned him national attention, with some analysts projecting him as a first-round NFL Draft pick. The team is ready to close out the regular season strong, but history warns against taking any opponent lightly. A Familiar Warning From 2017 History offers a stark reminder for Miami fans about the dangers of complacency. In 2017, the Hurricanes entered their final regular-season game with a 10-0 record and a 15-game winning streak. They were ranked No. 2 in the nation and had already clinched a spot in the conference title game. Facing a 4-7 Pittsburgh team with nothing to play for, Miami suffered a shocking 24-14 defeat. The loss ended their undefeated season and derailed their playoff hopes. That season ended with a 38-3 loss to Clemson in the championship game. Miami must avoid a repeat of that nightmare scenario this Saturday. The current Boston College team shares some DNA with that 2017 Pittsburgh squad. top.title: JJ Abrams’ Sci-Fi Thriller Found-Footage Masterpiece Is Being Removed From Paramount Plus
top.description: In some ways, the best found-footage movie ever made is still The Blair Witch Project . This wasn’t because of the film’s actual quality, but because of the effect it had on audiences back in 1999. When it was released, found-footage movies just weren't a well-known thing and the marketing campaign for the movie made it seem as though the events depicted actually happened. Since then, better found-footage movies have been made that have replay value — a quality The Blair Witch Project sorely lacks — but none since have ever tricked audiences quite so effectively.

top.title: Hall of Fame Poll: Brett Gardner
top.description: NEW YORK, NEW YORK - OCTOBER 01: Brett Gardner #11 of the New York Yankees in action against the Tampa Bay Rays at Yankee Stadium on October 01, 2021 in New York City. Tampa Bay Rays defeated the New York Yankees 4-3. (Photo by Mike Stobe/Getty Images) | Getty Images Happy Thanksgiving to those of you on the other side of our border. Happy Football day to the rest of us. The Jays are unlikely to make news today, so we’ll have a couple of non-news type posts today. Going alphabetically now the Hall of Fame ballot, the next three are really candidates: Asdrúbal Cabrera had a very nice career, playing 15 seasons in the MLB with a 30.0 WAR, hitting .266/.329/.423 with a 193 home run, 91 steals and a 30.0 bWAR. He played for eight teams: eight years with Cleveland, three each with the Mets and Nationals, and one with the Rays, Rangers, Diamondbacks, Phillies, and Reds. He made two All-Star teams, got MVP votes one (finishing 20th) and one Silver Slugger. He really didn’t have any real standout years, his best season had a 4.7 bWAR. He never drove in 100 runs (topped out at 92), also topped out at 25 home runs. A nice career but well short of a being a real Hall of Fame candidate. Starlin Castro played 12 seasons in the MLB, with a .280/.319/.412 batting line, 138 home runs and 678 RBI. He made four All-Star games, got MVP votes once (finishing 23rd in voting) and finished 5th in Rookie of the Year voting in 2010. In his best season he has a 3.5 bWAR. Wade Davis (I worked with a Wade Davis, I don’t think this is the same guy) played 13 seasons in the MLB and he did have a couple of good years, getting 43 saves in 2018 and 32 in 2017. But then he only had fourish season as a full time closer (and in one of those he had a 8.65 ERA). He pitched in 557 games, 88 starts, had a 63-55 record, 141 saves, a 3.94 ERA and a 10.2 bWAR. He made three All-Star teams, got Cy Young Votes twice (8th and 6th), MVP votes once (28th), and finished 4th in Rookie of the Year voting in 2009. Mark Gardner is closer to a real Hall of Fame candidate. He played 14 seasons with the Yankees (the cynic in me wants to say that any player who plays 14 years with the Yankees gets in the Hall). He played in 1688 games, had a .256/.342/.398 line, with 139 home runs, 274 steals and a 44.3 bWAR. In his best season, 2010 he had a 7.4 bWAR (his only season with a bWAR above 5). He made one All-Star Team and won one Gold Glove. He has one World Series ring (he hit .000/.000/.000 in the World Series) and played 68 playoff games, with a .211/.284/.281 batting line (which really doesn’t help his case). He led the league in steals once and triples once. When I saw his name, I really thought he would have more of a case for the Hall.

nigeria.title: Delta attack: PANDEF writes IGP, DSS DG, demands probe
nigeria.description: By Henry Umoru ABUJA — The Pan Niger Delta Forum (PANDEF) has written to the Inspector-General of Police, Olatunji Disu, and the Director-General of the Department of State Services (DSS), Oluwatosin Ajayi, demanding an urgent investigation into the reported violence at a political rally in Ughelli, Delta State. The socio-political organisation called on both security chiefs to work with other relevant agencies to identify and prosecute those who allegedly planned, sponsored, instigated or participated in the attack on the campaign train of former Deputy President of the Senate, Senator Ovie Omo-Agege. Omo-Agege, who is the All Progressives Congress (APC) senatorial candidate for Delta Central, was reportedly attacked during a campaign rally on Monday, November 23, 2026, with some persons said to have been killed and several others injured. In a letter signed by its National Chairman, Ambassador Godknows Igali, PANDEF strongly condemned the incident and described the reported loss of lives and injuries as disturbing and unacceptable. The organisation also urged the Federal Government, relevant federal agencies and the Delta State Government to provide financial and other forms of assistance to families of those reportedly killed, as well as adequate medical care for the injured. In the letter, PANDEF said it was shocked by reports of violence at a political rally organised by the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) in parts of Uduere, Delta State, on Monday. It, however, noted that the reports of deaths and injuries had yet to be officially corroborated. “According to media reports, which are yet to be officially corroborated, some persons reportedly lost their lives, while several others sustained varying degrees of injuries. We consider these reported incidents extremely disturbing and totally unacceptable,” the letter stated. PANDEF recalled that it had issued a statement the previous week warning against political violence, intimidation and intolerance of opposition parties in the South-South. It said the latest incident, coming days after its appeal, was a source of grave concern, adding that the region had traditionally upheld political tolerance, sportsmanship and civility. The organisation further warned that insecurity in the South-South could have implications beyond the region, given its strategic importance to Nigeria’s oil and gas industry and national economy. “Any disruption of peace and security in the region, particularly violence associated with political and electoral activities, could have far-reaching implications, not only for the safety and wellbeing of our people but also for the stability and economic survival of the country,” it said. nigeria.title: Tinubu willing to grant more interviews to Nigerian journalists — Bwala
nigeria.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Special Adviser to the President on Media and Policy Communication, Daniel Bwala, has said President Bola Tinubu is willing to grant more interviews to Nigerian journalists, while maintaining that the Presidency will decide which media organisations interview him. Bwala said this during an interview on the Niger Unfiltered podcast, published on Thursday, following questions about why Tinubu had granted only one official interview to Nigerian media organisations in about three years and seven months in office. “I expect us to do more. And the second time, you’ll see more of that,” Bwala said. He acknowledged that some interviews had been postponed at short notice, saying the President had sometimes agreed to meet journalists before later rescheduling. “There are a number of times in which the President called for media. At the 11th hour, he may have been advised, and then he would apologise and say some other time,” Bwala said. The presidential aide said Tinubu was willing to speak with journalists and did not need prepared answers or prior briefings before interviews. “There is a willingness to grant interviews on the part of the President. And the President, when granting interviews, didn’t need to read anything, didn’t need to be briefed,” he said. Bwala defended the Presidency’s right to choose the journalists and platforms it engages, saying it should not be pressured to grant interviews to specific media organisations. “We control our narrative. We decide who we grant interviews to. Nobody can come and tell us, grant to this one and not the other one,” he said. He said State House press corps members representing mainstream, new, social and print media covered the President’s daily activities. “In the State House press corps, we have representatives of the mainstream, the new media, the social media, and the print media. So every day, the activity of the President is covered by them,” Bwala said. He also criticised some media practitioners over what he described as political bias and a lack of professionalism, arguing that Tinubu should engage journalists capable of conducting balanced interviews. Bwala’s remarks followed criticism of Tinubu’s recent interview with American political strategist and media personality Diana London. Some Nigerians questioned why the President had granted an interview to a foreign media personality while rarely speaking with Nigerian journalists. The controversy grew after reports linked London to a $4.5 million lobbying arrangement involving a United States-based firm engaged by the Nigerian government. London denied receiving the money from the Federal Government or anyone in Nigeria, saying she travelled to Nigeria to interview Tinubu for a documentary. Former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar also challenged Tinubu to grant a live interview to Nigerian journalists and called for the release of the full, unedited recording of his conversation with London. nigeria.title: FCCPC urges supermarkets to protect consumer trust
nigeria.description: The Federal Competition and Consumer Protection Commission (FCCPC) has urged supermarket and shopping mall operators across the country to strengthen consumer protection practices and earn customers’ trust through transparent business operations. The Executive Vice Chairman of the commission, Mr Tunji Bello, gave the advice through the Lagos Zonal Coordinator, Dr Olubunmi Otti, at a one-day sectoral roundtable on compliance and enforcement of the Federal Competition and Consumer Protection Act (FCCPA) 2018, held in Lagos. The engagement, themed, “Compliance Obligations of Supermarket Operators,” was organised to sensitise operators on their responsibilities under the law, particularly as the yuletide shopping season approaches. Bello said supermarkets had become essential to millions of Nigerians, serving as major outlets for purchasing food, medicines, children’s necessities and other household essentials. He said customers placed their health, money and trust in the hands of supermarket operators whenever they patronised their businesses, adding that such trust must be protected. “The supermarket is no longer just a shop for millions of Nigerians; it is where they buy their food, medicine, children’s needs and daily essentials. “When a consumer walks into your store, they are placing their trust, their health and hard-earned money in your hands. That trust must be protected,” he said. The FCCPC boss said the FCCPA 2018 empowered the commission to protect consumers, promote fair competition and ensure that businesses operated transparently and accountably. He said the roundtable focused on the commission’s role in guiding compliance, consumer rights under the Act, safety standards in retail outlets, the legal framework and complaint resolution mechanisms. Bello disclosed that the commission received complaints daily concerning the supermarket sector, including discrepancies between shelf prices and prices charged at checkout points, the sale of expired or nearly expired products without clear disclosure, misleading promotions and discounts, poor refund and return policies, and inadequate product information. He cited the experience of a mother who budgeted N50,000 for monthly shopping but encountered higher prices at the payment counter, describing such discrepancies as a breach of consumer trust rather than a mere mistake. He said the commission’s objective was to reduce and ultimately eliminate such complaints, not to shut down businesses, but to help operators understand and comply with their obligations. “Compliance is not a burden; compliance is good business,” he said, adding that customers who trusted a supermarket’s products and refund policies were more likely to return. The engagement attracted representatives of supermarket and retail businesses, including Justrite Superstores, Jendol Superstores, Prince Ebeano Supermarkets, Sundry Foods and Edichat Pharmacy and Stores. nigeria.title: Igbokoda crash: Tinubu approves N100m, three-bedroom houses for victims’ families
nigeria.description: By Kingsley Omonobi President Bola Tinubu has approved three-bedroom flats in Abuja for the families of the 25 people who died in the October 5, 2026 Nigerian Air Force aircraft crash. He also announced the award of the sum of N100 million to the families of each military personnel who died in the crash, separate from the houses. The President made the announcement on Thursday during a memorial service and wreath-laying ceremony held in honour of the victims of the NAF ATR 42 aircraft accident. He said the houses, located in the Renewed Hope Housing Project in Abuja, would be allocated to the immediate families of the deceased military personnel and civilians who were aboard the aircraft. Tinubu described the housing allocation as a demonstration of the nation’s appreciation for the sacrifices of the fallen personnel. “As a tangible expression of the nation’s gratitude, I approve the allocation of three-bedroom flats in the Renewed Hope Housing Project in Abuja to the family of each of the military personnel who lost their lives in this accident. “No home can ever replace the one you have lost, but they gave their lives for Nigeria, and Nigeria will give their family a home,” he said. The president pointed out that the gesture would also be extended to the immediate families of the civilians on board the aircraft. “In addition to the flats, these officers would receive from this government N100m each,” he said. He assured the bereaved families that the government would remain committed to supporting them beyond the memorial ceremony. “Long after the wreaths have faded, our commitment to these families must remain evergreen,” Tinubu said. The president also assured Nigerians that the October 5 aircraft crash would be thoroughly investigated, promising that the findings would inform improvements in military and civilian aviation safety. “I assure the grieving nation that this accident will be thoroughly investigated. We will seek answers. We will learn the lessons. We will strengthen our military and civilian aviation safety standards. Our operational procedures and our institutional accountability will be strengthened. “We owe them the truth, and we will honour that debt,” he said. Tinubu further reaffirmed his administration’s commitment to improving the welfare, safety and operational capacity of the Armed Forces through modernisation, training and better equipment. “A nation that asks its sons and daughters to fly into danger must give them the best wings it can build,” he added. The president urged the bereaved families to remember the deceased for their service and contributions to the country, assuring them that their sacrifices would remain in the nation’s memory. The October 5 accident claimed the lives of 25 people, including military personnel and civilians. nigeria.title: Kwara Jailbreak: How negligence, insecurity aided inmates’ escape from 112-year-old Ilorin prison
nigeria.description: By Demola Akinyemi, Ilorin The jailbreak at the Correctional Centre, Oke-Kura, Ilorin, Kwara State, in the wee hours of last week Wednesday (November 18, 2026) exposed negligence, compromise of the staff and obsolete security equipment, according to Vanguard investigations. Sources at the centre confided in Vanguard that seven condemned prison inmates actually planned their escape, out of which two – Segun and Abraham – now declared wanted, were lucky. They had been planning their escape for about seven months. The rooms of the condemned prison inmates are said to be secluded and often dark, as they’re not supposed to go out like others. Vanguard also gathered that once in a while, when the condemned inmates go out to do social services, they are always heavily guarded. It was further gathered that for the seven months, they used a chisel to gradually opened the wall of their room, to create enough hole space for them to escape into the premises. Vanguard also gathered that they used posters to cover the space (inside and outside) so that no staff could easily notice their escape plan. It was further gathered that the Correctional Centre fence, about 17 feet high, was topped with embedded broken glass rather than a wire mesh. Furthermore, there is no CCTV camera covering inmates’ movements. D-Day On the day of escape, they got thick blankets which they tied together to make a long thick rope, and hooked it to the broken glasses on top of the fence. It was with this blanket-rope that the condemned inmates climbed over the tall fence and escaped to the other side, said a source. But after Segun and Abraham had scaled the fence, the blanket became weak. So it gave way, and the other five would-be escapees fell back on the prison premises. Vanguard also gathered that fully armed officers of the center, who were supposed to be on 24/7 surveillance to secure the other side of the fence, weren’t there to arrest the condemned inmates. It was during the morning roll call on Wednesday that the Correctional Centre staff on duty discovered that two condemned inmates had escaped. For instance, the centre was constructed in 1914 to accommodate 150 inmates but currently houses over 1,000. Vanguard further gathered that the staff in Ilorin Correctional Centre do not also match up with the overcrowded inmates. Of particular note is the lack of CCTV cameras to provide effective surveillance on the inmates, which also confirmed lack of security, and intelligent failures of the authorities. nigeria.description: By Angel Aniobi Oyo State Governor, Seyi Makinde has revealed that he bought a book and ovulation kits with his wife in their attempt to have a male child after welcoming two daughters. Makinde made this disclosure during an interview with media personality Chude Jideonwo, where he spoke about his family, fatherhood and the decision to have a third child. Recounting how they planned their family, the governor said he initially wanted just one child but reluctantly agreed to have two after his wife questioned why they should have only one. According to him, he was comfortable with having two daughters and did not consider the gender of his children important. “Gender doesn’t mean anything to me because I felt whether a girl or a boy, it’s all linked up to how you’re going to bring them up and how you set them up to impact their environment, and you can do it with any kid,” he said. Makinde, however, explained that cultural expectations and comments from his mother-in-law amplified his wife’s desire to have a male child. He said his mother-in-law told his wife that Yoruba men whose wives did not give birth to boys could seek to have a male child outside their marriages. “I’m a Yoruba man, but I think I am okay with the girls that God has blessed us with,” he recalled saying. The governor disclosed that it took more than five years for him to understand his wife’s desire to have a son, after which they agreed to explore ways of having a male child. He said he subsequently purchased a book on how to conceive a boy, which they both read and followed, alongside purchasing ovulation kits. “So, I said, okay, well, that’s fine. We have to go and buy a book on how to have a boy, and then we’ll read it and apply strictly,” he said. Makinde added that their efforts eventually resulted in the birth of their son, who became their third child. “That was it. nigeria.title: Driver Arrested Over Crash, Inferno That Killed 31 In Egypt
nigeria.description: Egyptian prosecutors announced on Thursday the arrest of a man accused of causing a massive fire that erupted when a fuel tanker overturned on a packed highway in Cairo, killing 31 people . The prosecution said the man had “admitted” to speeding when his car collided with the tanker, “causing the steering wheel to slip from his hands and his car to veer off course”. When the car hit the truck, one of its tyres exploded, causing it to overturn, the prosecution said. The fire erupted as a result of a petrol leak, it added. More than 20 million people live in Greater Cairo, a sprawling and dense metropolis. With its informal residential areas and often dilapidated infrastructure, Egypt has suffered several deadly fires in recent years. Car crashes are common and often blamed on reckless driving, poor maintenance, and uneven law enforcement, with traffic laws also being widely flouted. Last year, nearly 6,000 people died in road accidents across the country, according to Egypt’s state statistics agency. nigeria.title: WhatsApp to allow users schedule messages – here’s how you can
nigeria.description: WhatsApp has introduced a scheduled messaging feature that allows users to compose messages in advance and choose when they should be delivered, addressing one of the most requested additions to the messaging platform. The feature will enable users to schedule messages between 10 minutes and 14 days ahead in both individual and group chats. Announcing the update, WhatsApp said the feature would allow users to write messages when they think of them and have them delivered at a more appropriate time. “That’s why we’re introducing scheduled messages – one of our most requested features. You can write a message when you think of it and send it anywhere from 10 minutes to 14 days later, in both your 1:1 and group chats,” the company said. According to WhatsApp, scheduled messages will appear in recipients’ chats like ordinary messages, without any indication that they were composed and scheduled earlier. Users will also be able to view all their scheduled messages and delete them before delivery if they change their minds. How to schedule messages on WhatsApp To schedule a message on WhatsApp, users can follow these steps: Open WhatsApp and select an individual or group chat. Type the message they want to send. Press and hold the send button. Select the preferred date and time for the message to be delivered. Confirm the schedule. The message will then be delivered automatically at the selected time. WhatsApp said scheduled messages would still be delivered even if the sender’s phone was switched off or ran out of battery. The feature will support text messages, photographs and videos, giving users the option to plan different types of communication ahead of time. The company also assured users that scheduled messages would retain WhatsApp’s end-to-end encryption, meaning only the sender and intended recipients would be able to read them. “Even if your phone is off or out of battery, your scheduled message will still show up at the time you chose, and it remains end-to-end encrypted like all your personal messages, so no one else can read it, not even us,” WhatsApp said. The scheduled messaging feature is rolling out globally over the coming weeks, although the company did not specify when it would become available to all users. WhatsApp said the update was another way for users to stay connected with important people by ensuring their messages arrive at exactly the right time. business.title: Bitcoin Has Become Boring, Finally
business.description: Bitcoin Magazine Bitcoin Has Become Boring, Finally The 2019 Lightning conference in Berlin was lit: five hundred “cypherpunks” getting each other high on visions of a future with peer-to-peer electronic cash. Attending a bitcoin conference back in the day felt like being a teenager at a friend’s party while their parents were out of town. It was exciting and new. The feeling was the opposite of FOMO: something big was happening, we were on the inside, and the rest of the world was going to envy us. It was the kind of party that you could only have when the adults weren’t looking. Whenever someone bought a beer (with bitcoin), everyone would hoot and holler and record it on their phones for Instagram/Twitter (it was still called Twitter). Lightning was the bleeding edge. We called it “the Lightning Network” (capitalized, if you please), and talking about it felt like talking about string theory: something so far out you’re not even sure it’s real. I spent a lot of time invoking the abacus . Those are the times some of us remember fondly and keep trying to relive at bitcoin conferences today. That’s why we engage in rituals like drone shows, Satoshi Rockamoto sets, beefsteak dinners , and video game tournaments for sats, but it’s not the same. The ratio of bitcoin OG speakers to suits is shifting. Many event rooms are half empty, and the halls and meeting rooms are full of people negotiating cap tables and profit-sharing splits. The adults haven’t shut the party down, but they have crashed it, and it kinda feels like their party now. The most exciting thing I noticed at the last bitcoin conference I attended was that nothing exciting happened. And that’s worth celebrating. From Tech Subcultures to Mainstream Tech Adoption The road to boring is seldom smooth. Technological innovation benefits from passion and bold ideas. People work harder on a project when they feel strongly about it and identify closely with like-minded collaborators. That’s where tech subcultures, their rituals, and their dogmas come from. But such passion and tribalism feed conflict, at least for a while until the tech goes mainstream, and normies, who couldn’t care less about subculture squabbles, take over. This progression from an exciting new technology that inspires strong emotions to a humdrum utility is not unusual. World-changing innovations often (always?) start with a committed subculture that identifies fiercely with their weird tech before the mainstream adopts it and soon expects it. In fact, this trajectory has become the standard doctrine of tech marketing. entertainment.description: What makes a good teacher? Beyond knowing a subject, a good teacher can understand students, inspire confidence, and help young people discover what they are capable of becoming. It was this broader responsibility of educators that Dr. Tunji Olowolafe explored while delivering the 2026 Convocation Lecture at the Sikiru Adetona College of Education, Science and Technology (SACOETEC), Omu-Ajose, Ogun State. Speaking on Monday, 23 November 2026, on the theme “The Dual-Mandate NCE-Degree Programme: Prospects, Challenges and the Future of Teacher Education in Nigeria,” he described the programme as an important opportunity to reposition teacher education. For decades, Colleges of Education depended on university affiliations to award Bachelor’s degrees, despite many possessing the academic capacity to run such programmes. The Federal Colleges of Education Act 2023 changed this, empowering eligible institutions to award degrees independently. Under the Dual-Mandate programme, students can complete three years of NCE training and proceed to another two years for a Bachelor’s degree in Education. Dr. Olowolafe explained that combining practical teaching skills with deeper academic knowledge would produce better-prepared educators. However, he cautioned that institutional autonomy must be supported by sustained funding, improved curricula and professional development. With Nigeria facing an estimated shortage of one million teachers, he also called for greater integration of vocational education, artificial intelligence and digital skills into learning. “AI can explain a quadratic equation at midnight, but it cannot offer the steady, empathetic guidance of a caring adult,” he said, emphasizing that artificial intelligence must complement, not replace, the human qualities of effective teaching. During the lecture, Dr. Olowolafe announced that the Tunji Olowolafe Foundation would establish a fully equipped, solar-powered Gbemisola Olowolafe Memorial ICT Centre (GOMTECH) with high-speed internet connectivity at SACOETEC. The Foundation is also committed to recognising academic excellence and outstanding teaching at the College. This includes recognising the College’s first-class degree graduates and NCE distinction holders, alongside the overall best NCE and degree graduates. Lecturers, selected based on student ratings, will also be honoured for their teaching contributions. The initiative builds on the Foundation’s existing investment in education, including Project Digi-Teach at Ekiti State University and GOMTECH in Are-Ekiti. For Dr. Olowolafe, the commitment to educators is also deeply personal. His mother was a teacher, his elder sister taught for years at Baptist Academy, Lagos, and his late wife, Gbemisola Olowolafe, was a lifelong educator. Then you probably remember that voice. Deep, commanding and unmistakable, it often came with his signature red cap, traditional Igbo attire and a generous helping of proverbs. The actor was just as memorable away from the screen, where his sharp wit, outspoken nature and candid opinions made him a fascinating personality in interviews. He was never one to shy away from saying exactly what he thought, and that straightforwardness became another part of what audiences remembered about him. For generations of Nollywood viewers, Pete Edochie was the actor they could recognise before he had even finished his first sentence. He became one of Nigerian cinema’s most familiar faces, often playing kings, chiefs, fathers and respected elders. His breakthrough came in 1987 when he portrayed Okonkwo in the television adaptation of Chinua Achebe ‘s Things Fall Apart , a performance that helped establish him as one of Nollywood’s most respected actors. Directed by David Orere , the acclaimed television miniseries marked Edochie’s first professional acting role and saw him bring the proud, fierce, and deeply conflicted Umuofia warrior to life with remarkable nuance. entertainment.title: Nollywood Legend Pete Edochie Passes Away at 79
entertainment.description: Nollywood icon Pete Edochie, MON, who passed away at the age of 79 in Enugu. Photo Credit: Pete Edochie/Instagram Nollywood and the wider African entertainment community are mourning the loss of one of their most respected screen icons, Pete Edochie , MON, who passed away on Wednesday, 25 November 2026,at the age of 79. According to an official statement released on behalf of the family by his eldest son, Leo Pete Edochie , the veteran actor and retired broadcaster departed this life at 12:30 a.m. in Enugu, Nigeria, following a protracted battle with prostate cancer. Born on 7 March 1947 in Zaria, Kaduna State, and hailing from Akamnato, Ifite Nteje in Anambra State, Pete Edochie began his career in broadcasting long before becoming a household name on television and cinema screens. At age 20, in 1967, he joined the Eastern Nigeria Broadcasting Service (ENBS)—later the Anambra Broadcasting Service (ABS)—rising steadily through the ranks to serve as Director of Programmes and Deputy Managing Director. His defining breakthrough came in 1987 when he portrayed the fierce, tragic hero Okonkwo in the Nigerian Television Authority’s (NTA) acclaimed television adaptation of Chinua Achebe ‘s Things Fall Apart. His commanding presence and deep, resonant voice earned him international recognition—including a dedicated delegation interview from the BBC—and cemented his place in Nigerian television history. Over a screen career spanning nearly four decades, Pete Edochie became synonymous with authority,traditional wisdom, and unforgettable Igbo proverbs. Whether playing stern monarchs, principled elders, or complex patriarchs, he delivered every line with unmistakable gravitas. His extensive filmography includes standout appearances in classics and modern hits alike, such as Things Fall Apart (1987), Igodo (1999), Egg of Life (2003), Oracle (2003), Billionaires Club (2003), End of Money (2005), Lionheart (2018)—where he starred as Chief Ernest Obiagu alongside Genevieve Nnaji—Unroyal (2020), and Foreigner’s God (2022). In recognition of his immense contributions to Nigerian arts and culture, he was conferred with the national honour of Member of the Order of the Niger (MON) in 2003 by former President Olusegun Obasanjo,alongside the Africa Magic Viewers’ Choice Awards (AMVCA) Industry Merit Award and lifetime achievement honours from the Africa Film Academy and the African Film Festival (TAFF). Cricket Ireland on Thursday confirmed that the team will arrive in Pakistan on January 9 for a series running from January 13 to 24, with all six matches to be played at the Gaddafi Stadium in Lahore. The tour will comprise three 50-over matches against Pakistan A, known as the Shaheens, followed by a three-match ODI series against the senior Pakistan side. sports.title: How a baseball coach helped build a national esports contender at Choctaw
sports.description: For Oklahoma’s Choctaw High School esports team, everything has happened pretty quickly. At the beginning of last school year, the newly minted program had a few students trickling in, some interest here and there. Just one season later, the Yellowjackets are ranked No. 25 in the nation and sitting at fourth in the USA TODAY Sports esports national title race. Talk about a bit of a jump. “It’s just kind of finding the right pieces to put the puzzle together,” said head coach Tim Ackerman, who has built the team up over the past year. “Everyone here has been super, super helpful every step of the way.” Ackerman spent years as a high school baseball coach, a role he still reprises each spring, before taking up the mantle as Choctaw’s inaugural esports leader. He’s infused some of that more traditional coaching experience, namely his emphasis on competitive practice, into his new role. “I’ve got really good gamers here who know a lot about their games, play their games well. But when it comes down to it, I think competing is a very important gap that a lot of schools miss on,” Ackerman said. “Understanding how to control momentum, how to control your emotions as you go…a professional approach when you’re going into a match, rather than just you’re at home with a controller.” View this post on Instagram It took a minute for the program to find its footing, but over time, students who might not have been attracted to it at first glance started to trickle in. They’d pop their heads into Ackerman’s room, telling him about their favorite games and scoring invites to “show me what you got” as he collected the right players for the team. Senior Blake Wallace, the team’s "Marvel Rivals" captain, was convinced to give it a shot though it did take second. “When I saw it my sophomore year in the classes you could take, I was like, ‘Only nerds are going to take that. I’m not going to do that,” Wallace said. But he came around. Now as a captain, he’s helped chart the course for the ever-growing squad. “My favorite part is that we’re always improving,” he said. “We do things where we go through games we lost and just break down everything we did wrong, and what we could do better next game.” The success and popularity of Choctaw’s esports squad has already extended to the middle school level, where Ackerman said nearly 70 students tried out for the small number of spots available on the Choctaw teams there. “I think the future is pretty bright over here,” he said. “There’s a lot of really excited, good players coming in, showing interest and wanting to be a part of it.” Meet the Choctaw team "Rocket League" Talan Wilkins Marco Torres Matthew Hernandez "Marvel Rivals" Grayson Cornelius Jaxon Buckingham Nik Hofmaier Daryl Knauer Sean Grizzle Blake Wallace "Madden NFL 27" Dashaun Taylor This article originally appeared on USA TODAY: How a baseball coach helped build a national esports contender at Choctaw

sports.title: Hall of Fame Poll: Brett Gardner
sports.description: NEW YORK, NEW YORK - OCTOBER 01: Brett Gardner #11 of the New York Yankees in action against the Tampa Bay Rays at Yankee Stadium on October 01, 2021 in New York City. Tampa Bay Rays defeated the New York Yankees 4-3. (Photo by Mike Stobe/Getty Images) | Getty Images Happy Thanksgiving to those of you on the other side of our border. Happy Football day to the rest of us. The Jays are unlikely to make news today, so we’ll have a couple of non-news type posts today. Going alphabetically now the Hall of Fame ballot, the next three are really candidates: Asdrúbal Cabrera had a very nice career, playing 15 seasons in the MLB with a 30.0 WAR, hitting .266/.329/.423 with a 193 home run, 91 steals and a 30.0 bWAR. He played for eight teams: eight years with Cleveland, three each with the Mets and Nationals, and one with the Rays, Rangers, Diamondbacks, Phillies, and Reds. He made two All-Star teams, got MVP votes one (finishing 20th) and one Silver Slugger. He really didn’t have any real standout years, his best season had a 4.7 bWAR. He never drove in 100 runs (topped out at 92), also topped out at 25 home runs. A nice career but well short of a being a real Hall of Fame candidate. Starlin Castro played 12 seasons in the MLB, with a .280/.319/.412 batting line, 138 home runs and 678 RBI. He made four All-Star games, got MVP votes once (finishing 23rd in voting) and finished 5th in Rookie of the Year voting in 2010. In his best season he has a 3.5 bWAR. Wade Davis (I worked with a Wade Davis, I don’t think this is the same guy) played 13 seasons in the MLB and he did have a couple of good years, getting 43 saves in 2018 and 32 in 2017. But then he only had fourish season as a full time closer (and in one of those he had a 8.65 ERA). He pitched in 557 games, 88 starts, had a 63-55 record, 141 saves, a 3.94 ERA and a 10.2 bWAR. He made three All-Star teams, got Cy Young Votes twice (8th and 6th), MVP votes once (28th), and finished 4th in Rookie of the Year voting in 2009. Mark Gardner is closer to a real Hall of Fame candidate. He played 14 seasons with the Yankees (the cynic in me wants to say that any player who plays 14 years with the Yankees gets in the Hall). He played in 1688 games, had a .256/.342/.398 line, with 139 home runs, 274 steals and a 44.3 bWAR. In his best season, 2010 he had a 7.4 bWAR (his only season with a bWAR above 5). He made one All-Star Team and won one Gold Glove. He has one World Series ring (he hit .000/.000/.000 in the World Series) and played 68 playoff games, with a .211/.284/.281 batting line (which really doesn’t help his case). He led the league in steals once and triples once. When I saw his name, I really thought he would have more of a case for the Hall.

James scored 14 consecutive points in the second quarter, including three straight threes, to help Philadelphia seize control. He later threw a half-court alley-oop to VJ Edgecombe and sealed the triple-double with a rebound in the final two minutes, drawing a standing ovation. At 41, he also became the oldest player in NBA history to record a triple-double, breaking his own record. “If they need me to dust off the cape from time to time, I can still accomplish that,” James said afterward. sports.title: He is the player who has the most Davis Cup wins in history who never won the title
sports.description: The Davis Cup is now officially underway, as Italy are bidding to make history by becoming the first team ever to win a record fourth straight titles. However, this year, they will arguably face their fiercest competition yet, especially given Jannik Sinner is absent, having undergone knee surgery just days ago. Italy has a supremely rich history regarding this tournament, though it took them until 1976 to finally claim a maiden title. And, interestingly, the man who led them to that silverware as captain remains technically the most successful player in the history of the Davis Cup . That is, despite Nicola Pietrangeli actually never winning the tournament as a player. Nicola Pietrangeli – the greatest player to have never won the Davis Cup? Whilst it’s hard to brand a player as the most successful in an event’s history without ever actually winning it, the Davis Cup is unique compared to the rest of the tennis tour. After all, it is a team event, and one special player cannot win it on his own. Photo by Andreas SOLARO / AFP via Getty Images Pietrangeli certainly gave it his all across a glittering career, where he won two Roland Garros titles in the 1970s. However, the Davis Cup sadly always eluded him, despite leading his team to two finals. On both occasions, they lost to a strong Australian side on grass. Pietrangeli retired having amassed the most total wins (120, 78 singles, 42 doubles) and having played the most ties (66). He had to wait until 1976 to eventually lift the trophy, four years after he called time on his career. He did so as the captain of the Italian Davis Cup team. Who else has the most wins in Davis Cup history? Whilst Pietrangeli might lead the way when it comes to most singles wins, most ties played and most wins in total, there are a number of notable stars who trail him. In second place is Ilie Năstase, the legendary Romanian star who snagged two major titles during an era boasting legends like Rod Laver, Arthur Ashe, Jon Newcombe and Ken Rosewall. Rank Player Total W–L Singles W–L Ties played 1 Nicola Pietrangeli (ITA) 120–44 78–32 66 2 Ilie Năstase (ROU) 109–37 74–22 52 3 Omar Alawadhi (UAE) 104–54 66–33 – 4 Leander Paes (IND) 93–35 48–22 58 5 Manuel Santana (ESP) 92–28 69–17 46 He played 52 ties to Pietrangeli’s 66, winning 74 singles matches and winning just 11 fewer total matches than the Italian. Omar Alawadhi of the UAE sits in third, with Indian tennis legend Leander Paes in fourth. Manuel Santana rounds out the list in fifth.

sports.title: Barcelona Eyes Ayden Heaven Loan Amid Man United Struggles
sports.description: Aug 3, 2024; Columbia, South Carolina, USA; Liverpool and Manchester United players enter the field before their match at Williams-Brice Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Jeff Blake-USA TODAY Sports Barcelona have expressed interest in a January loan for Manchester United defender Ayden Heaven . The 20-year-old center-back has yet to appear in either of new manager Mauricio Pochettino’s matches and is open to leaving Old Trafford for regular game time. BBC Sport’s Nizaar Kinsella reported that Heaven prefers a loan but would also consider a permanent move. Fulham are also monitoring the situation. Both clubs tried to sign Heaven when he left Arsenal for United in February 2025. United have been linked with a center-back addition of their own, including Fulham’s Calvin Bassey, but the Cottagers view Bassey as important to their plans and are unlikely to facilitate any swap. Heaven was an unused substitute in Pochettino’s first game , the 4-0 defeat at Liverpool, and again in Wednesday’s 2-2 Champions League draw at Sporting CP. The young defender, who has made 32 senior appearances for United since joining, is now on his third permanent manager in 21 months. He accepts that Pochettino may lean on more experienced options as United sit 19th and fight to avoid relegation. United’s defensive issues have been clear. The Anfield loss featured a red card for Leny Yoro and individual errors; the Lisbon draw was chaotic, with multiple penalties, disallowed goals, and late drama. Heaven has watched both from the bench while the new coaching staff searches for stability. Barcelona’s interest is part of a broader January picture. Scouts from Juventus, Inter, AC Milan, Manchester City, Tottenham, and Arsenal watched Antonio Nusa score a brace in RB Leipzig’s 3-1 win over Lens. Leipzig are aware of the growing attention on the 21-year-old, whose contract runs until 2029. Liverpool, Manchester United, and Newcastle have also been linked with Juventus winger Francisco Conceição. Jorge Mendes offered the 23-year-old to Newcastle for next summer in a deal that could help Juventus secure Nick Woltemade permanently. Conceição has indicated he is focused on winning trophies at Juventus for now. Napoli have made the first move for Monza striker Gustavo Varela, with Inter, AC Milan, and Juventus also in the mix for the 21-year-old. Separately, intermediaries continue regular contact between Real Madrid and Barcelona as both clubs explore the possibility of a 2027 move for Manchester City’s Erling Haaland . Heaven’s situation is more immediate: a young player who wants minutes and clubs that have long liked his profile.

The Argentinian had been close to joining the Bianconeri, with an agreement reportedly in place for a loan move covering the current season. However, the proposed transfer depended on Juventus selling Juan Cabal first. Atalanta were interested in signing Cabal, and Cristiano Giuntoli wanted to complete the deal for Tagliafico once the Colombian’s departure had been arranged. Juventus were confident that everything would fall into place, but the situation changed as the transfer deadline approached. There was no serious progress from La Dea, and Cabal ultimately remained at Juventus. That prevented the Bianconeri from completing their move for Tagliafico , despite having worked towards an agreement with Lyon. Juventus still interested in Tagliafico The Bianconeri have not abandoned their interest in the left-back and are expected to continue trying to secure his signature. However, their pursuit could prove more complicated this time because additional clubs are now competing for the defender. Atletico Madrid were already competing with Juventus for the Argentinian during the summer window. Juve must now also contend with interest from clubs in Tagliafico’s home country, creating another challenge in their efforts to bring him to Turin. According to Tuttojuve , several Argentinian clubs are showing significant interest in the defender, with River Plate among the teams monitoring his situation. That interest could give Tagliafico an alternative to continuing his career in Europe. (Photo by Jose Manuel Alvarez Rey/Getty Images) River Plate could complicate Juventus’ plans At this stage of his career, the left-back may be open to returning to Argentina rather than remaining in European football. A move back home could therefore become a genuine possibility if the right opportunity presents itself. Juventus will need to make a concrete approach if they want to convince him to choose their project. Their previous agreement and interest could help, but they cannot assume that the defender will automatically favour a move to Turin over the alternatives available to him. It remains to be seen whether Tagliafico wants to stay in Europe with Juventus or considers a return to Argentina. The Bianconeri must also weigh up their options at left-back, especially as Cabal has been superb for them so far.

sports.title: Appreciating a Few New Jersey Devils Who Are Quietly Having a Good Season So Far
sports.description: DALLAS, TEXAS - OCTOBER 27: Connor Brown #16 and Brett Pesce #22 of the New Jersey Devils celebrate with Connor Hellebuyck #37 after the win over the Dallas Stars at American Airlines Center on October 27, 2026 in Dallas, Texas. (Photo by Richard Rodriguez/Getty Images) | Getty Images As we celebrate Thanksgiving in the United States today, it feels like a good time to look at a few potentially underappreciated New Jersey Devils this season. Oh sure, Jack Hughes is playing great, Jesper Bratt is almost a point per game, and Nico Hischier became the second Devil to hit double digit goals last night. You could look at Luke Hughes being fifth on the team in points and celebrate the step forward he’s taken, but again, these are the things that typically get brought up as Devils positives. We’re looking at unsung heroes today to sing their praises, and let’s start off with some who’s been piling up points since he entered the lineup this season. Connor Brown Brown’s 2026-27 definitely didn’t start how we wanted it to, as he missed the team’s first eight games due to injury. Since entering the lineup, Brown has been outstanding, contributing seven goals and six assists in 17 games. Across a full 84 game season that would be good for a 64 point pace, which would blow away his current career high of 43. Currently sixth in Devils scoring, Brown could still reach the 50 point plateau for the first time in his career if he’s able to keep up at least a similar scoring pace to the one he’s been on since his season debut. Connor looks quick and engaged on every shift, making him a dangerous player no matter where he finds himself in the team’s lineup. Brett Pesce While not known for his point contributions, Pesce is known for playing great shutdown defense and he’s done just that for the Devils. He continues to be deployed alongside Luke Hughes, which continues to allow the youngest Hughes brother the ability to be a little more offensively loose. Plus/minus isn’t the greatest indicator of a player’s on ice impact, but Pesce’s team leading +14 still demonstrates that he’s keeping the puck moving in the right direction more often than not. technology.description: Britain's privacy watchdog is getting a taste of its own medicine, with an independent review set to examine the culture, governance, and accountability surrounding the events that led to former Information Commissioner John Edwards' resignation. Karon Monaghan KC will examine whether the regulator's culture and governance allowed problems to develop or made concerns harder to raise. Edwards quit in June after an independent workplace investigation found there was a "case to answer" over his behavior and that his conduct fell short of what was expected of a public official. He disagreed with some of its findings, but ultimately conceded that he had shown "poor judgment." That investigation, however, focused on Edwards alone. According to the terms of reference published on Thursday, it "did not consider the wider conditions in which that conduct occurred, and it was not designed to." The new review will cast a wider net. Monaghan wants to know whether staff could call out bad behavior further up the food chain, and what awaited those who tried. It will also poke around the regulator's leadership and governance arrangements and its relationship with its sponsoring government department, including whether there were adequate ways for concerns to be escalated and those at the top to be challenged. Current and former staff can give evidence confidentially and voluntarily, while Monaghan will be given access to relevant documents and existing material, including staff surveys and data on bullying, harassment and discrimination. The ICO has confirmed it won't use confidentiality clauses in settlement agreements to prevent people from contributing to the review. Monaghan decides which witnesses and documents are relevant, rather than the ICO or DCMS. Access remains subject to legal restrictions, and she must be told when material is withheld and why. She can speak to whoever she thinks is relevant and ask for the complaints, correspondence, and other paperwork she needs. And if that leads her somewhere unexpected, she can ask to widen the investigation. DCMS can refuse, but it won't be able to quietly brush the request aside, and any decision not to expand the scope has to make it into the final report. The review won't reopen the investigation into Edwards, make findings about the conduct of named individuals, or delve into the merits of the regulator's enforcement decisions. Its arrival comes amid a broader shake-up at Britain's data watchdog. The old Information Commissioner's Office was formally replaced by the Information Commission on September 30, bringing with it a new board-led governance model. The government first promised the wider review in July, shortly after Edwards' departure, but it didn't appoint its reviewer or nail down the terms until late November. technology.title: Rackspace pulls plug on Spot cloud service after security breach
technology.description: Rackspace is shutting down its low-cost Spot cloud service after a security breach, giving customers two weeks' notice to move their workloads and retrieve their data. In a notice posted on Tuesday , the cloud computing biz said its Rackspace Spot service will cease operations at 1700 Central Time (2300 UTC) on December 8. Any workloads still running at that point will be terminated, and customers will no longer be able to access their data. "Following the recent security incident affecting Rackspace Spot, Rackspace has made the decision to wind down the service," the company said. "Spot customers are being notified with the wind-down timeline, instructions for retrieving their data and steps to secure their environments." Customers will have to contend with the fallout from the breach while simultaneously trying to get their applications and data off the platform. According to a customer notification seen by The Register , the attackers used leaked credentials to access parts of Rackspace Spot over a period of almost 22 hours on November 17. Rackspace only learned of the intrusion the following day, after a customer raised the alarm. The intruders impersonated legitimate users, created pods in customer Kubernetes clusters, gained access to stored credentials known as Kubernetes Secrets, and listed nodes and storage volumes. "With that access, they could have read any Secret in an affected user's clusters, and any Spot API token or refresh token that user held," Rackspace told customers. Rackspace has since revoked the affected tokens and sessions, removed the pods planted by the intruders, and changed the affected platform and storage keys. Customers must also reissue API tokens, download new Kubernetes configuration files, and rotate credentials stored in their clusters, including database passwords and third-party API keys. Sirish Raghuram, co-founder and chief growth officer of Platform9, which co-developed Spot with Rackspace, shed some light on the root cause in a November 20 GitHub post. "An observability system was breached using a compromised credential," Raghuram wrote. "This was obviously a critical error on our part and we are very sorry we let this happen." Raghuram said the incident necessitated significant changes to the underlying infrastructure clusters, prolonging the outage. Spot's selling point was cheap compute. The service operated an auction-based pricing model, allowing customers to bid for cloud infrastructure at a fraction of the cost of conventional on-demand instances. Rackspace advertised savings of up to 90 percent for customers willing to tolerate interruptions to their workloads. A permanent interruption probably wasn't what they had in mind. Rackspace hasn't explained why it chose closure over recovery, revealed how many customers were affected, or said whether it will offer migration extensions. It did not respond to The Register's questions. ®

technology.description: Peninsula Energy has temporarily shut down its Wyoming uranium operation after a "cybersecurity incident" affected plant and wellfield control systems. The Australian uranium producer said on Wednesday that it had activated its response procedures and brought in outside specialists following the attack on its US subsidiary, Strata Energy, which operates the Lance uranium project. Peninsula Energy said it believes the attack is "confined to the plant and wellfield operating and control systems," and that back-office functions, such as payroll and other corporate systems, in both the US and Australia, remain unaffected. "The company's immediate priorities have been to protect the safety of its employees, secure its operating systems, and work towards the restoration of operations in a safe and controlled manner," it said in an update to the Australian Securities Exchange. The notification [PDF] went on to say that Peninsula Energy's investigations into the attack, including whether any data was compromised, remain ongoing. Peninsula has not given a restart date and says it cannot yet assess the impact on its 2027 production guidance. Operations will remain suspended until recovery and safety checks are complete. "Peninsula will provide further updates to the market as material information becomes available," it said. The disclosure of additional information came two days after Peninsula secured a short trading halt, which referenced a cybersecurity incident at its Wyoming site. The November 23 filing [PDF] dated the incident to Friday evening in Western Australia. Wednesday's update clarified that Strata detected it on the morning of November 20, local US time. Peninsula subsequently requested a voluntary suspension of trading until the earlier of November 30 or an announcement on restarting operations and any resulting change to production guidance. Peninsula's Lance project is a uranium mining operation, extracting the element from underground deposits and turning it into uranium concentrate, aka yellowcake or U₃O₈. Uranium concentrate is feedstock for nuclear fuel production, typically undergoing conversion, enrichment, and fabrication into uranium dioxide pellets before use in reactors. The Lance central processing plant was constructed to produce a maximum of 2.0 million pounds (Mlb) of U₃O₈ annually, and is licensed for 3.0 Mlb.
